name: Theme
author: brodgar
description: Example addon (033-ui-stylesheet C1a, extended by 035-ui-chrome C2): A CLIENT THEME THAT IS DATA, NOT CODE — text AND chrome. Everything this addon looks like lives in theme.json next to main.lua — main.lua never names a surface, a font, a size, a colour or a pixel; it reads the file, maps the two values JSON cannot hold to handles, and hands the whole table to hafen.ui.skin{}. To make a different theme you edit the JSON. Three ordinary doors, one line each: hafen.asset('theme.json') is the FILE this addon ships (a 'data' asset, 033.3 — read as UTF-8 through :text(), sandboxed like every asset: absolute paths and '..' are rejected, D-017); hafen.json.parse turns the text into a table (a JSON array is 1-indexed, so [190,210,190] arrives as the sheet's own positional colour shape and needs no conversion); hafen.ui.skin{} installs it. EXACTLY TWO values in a rule are things JSON cannot carry, and both for the same reason — they are HANDLES: a font's `face` (a bare name is one of the client's built-ins, anything with a dot is a file this addon ships) and a border's or background's `image` (always a file this addon ships, here frame.png and panel.png). Both go through hafen.asset, the same door theme.json came through; a colour array, a 9-slice's four insets and a pad in pixels are already the sheet's own shapes and are copied verbatim, so the whole chrome half of the theme costs three lines of Lua. The chrome rules are the C2 half: 'window.frame' carries bg + a 9-slice border + pad, so every window wears a dark slate frame whose 40 px top inset IS the title band the caption sits in (the engine adds no hidden room for a caption — a theme that wants a title bar says so in its own top inset), and 'panel' carries a thinner border for the framed surfaces that are not windows (the portrait, party avatars, list/info boxes, petals, dropdowns), which cannot re-lay themselves out and therefore take no pad. DORMANT until you ask for it: ':theme on' wears it, ':theme off' takes it off, ':theme dump' lists what it styles, chrome included — a theme installed at login would restyle your whole client on every login, which is not an example addon's decision to make. The sheet is OWNED: :reload or disabling this addon drops it and the stock client comes back, and with a second styling addon the last one applied wins (D-043). Assets are interned, so an edit to theme.json takes effect on ':reload'. SAFE-tier: cosmetic, client-side, declares no permissions, sends nothing to the server.
